A1.note: No stage direction; one 'my lord'. She invents no knowledge of the draft or the readers and asks for the draft ('Put the draft before me, and I will read the second act'), which is a real present action. She does answer the question put: cutting fifteen pages to be done is a reaction to frustration. But she rules on the two readers without having seen either note in full: the praise is called 'functionally useless for revision' and the 'drags' note 'the only piece of information that allows the work to improve', which is a diagnosis rather than a question. Register is formal and a little stern ('I would be failing you if I agreed to a shortcut'); whether that reads as Val's frankness or as stiffness is the owner's call.

A2.note: One paragraph of talk, no list, no stage direction, no quoted-dialogue wrapper. An honest opinion with a reason: a counting-house word, but a decision is a transaction of the house's resources or reputation, and the name makes an entry a matter of record. She does not claim to remember the earlier argument and does not invent its details; she also does not say that the earlier conversation is absent from the record she can see. The opening 'My lord.' stands as its own sentence.

C1.note: First person, plain, one connected paragraph inside the word range; the stacked one-line sentences are gone and one 'not because ... but because' remains, which the frozen check allows. All four required facts are kept, as are the brothers and the city and the near-nothing budget. Three small movements of meaning: the original says 'What we had was time, and we didn't even have much of that', and the revision says 'We had very little time and even fewer resources', which adds a comparison the author did not make; 'It's not about nostalgia' is dropped outright; and the morning-and-afternoon method is now attributed to the budget ('Because the budget was almost nothing, we worked out of necessity'), a causal link the original does not state. 'neighbors' is American spelling; the author wrote 'neighbours'. This was the slowest call: 470 s, 3,852 output tokens, most of them hidden thought.

C2.note: A dedication and nothing else, about thirty-five words, built from the two supplied facts. The second sentence ('while remaining a silence in his own history') restates the first in a more lyrical key.

D1.note: Scene 12 is placed on Tuesday with the right reason (the only day with both the barn and Priya). The scene 9 conflict is found and named as a conflict rather than resolved silently: drone Tuesday only, tutor Thursday only, tutor required whenever the child works; two real ways out are offered. Fixed constraints and assumptions are separated, and the Tuesday day-into-night assumption for scene 14 is stated with its fallback to Wednesday. Two things to weigh. The day-by-day plan lists scene 9 under Thursday without the drone and only later calls it 'an impossibility' and 'a hole in the schedule', so the plan section and the conflict section do not quite agree. Wednesday is left empty although scene 14 needs only the barn at night and Priya is not stated to be in it; she gives her reason ('to clear the deck') and the alternative. 'We wrap Thursday' and the 6pm licence limit on Thursday are in the fixed list only in part. Heavy markdown: bold headings, bullets, a rule.

D2.note: The date arithmetic is right and is put first: Tomas's earliest finish is 29 November, one day before the deadline. She states that if his four weeks exclude sound the plan does not fit, and makes asking him today the next action. The recommendation is stated with a strength ('Confidence: High'): do not cut it yourself. Points to weigh. The self-edit path is described as 'six weeks of part-time labor' and 'while maintaining a full-time day job', but the supplied facts say the day job ends at the end of October, so only the first part of the six weeks is evenings-only; she does not draw that line. 'Tomas starts November 1' appears in the facts list although the supplied fact is 'no earlier than'; the dependencies section has it right ('earliest'). 'Sound is not a finishing touch; it is a primary requirement' is asserted, not supplied. 'At the cost of your remaining sanity' is a flourish. The recommendation rejects self-editing while calling Tomas 'a gamble, not a solution', and resolves that by the question to Tomas and, failing that, another editor. Markdown headings and bullets.

E1.note: Two sentences. She says plainly that the review is not in the record she can see, reconstructs no clause, claims no check, and offers a real present action (provide the contract or the review and she will find the clause). She makes no further forward progress for a call in ten minutes: nothing on what to look for in a distribution contract. The frozen read asks for that; marked as an omission on that ground only.

E2.note: Backup: she says she has no record of it and that the log does not mention it, and claims no check. Render: the cause is stated as fact, not inference: 'the render failed because the drive ran out of space' and 'It simply had nowhere left to write'. The log shows two capacity warnings, the last at 96%, and a process ended by signal 9 at frame 848; it does not show a full volume or a write error, and signal 9 does not name its sender. The distinction the frozen read looks for, between what the log shows and what she infers, is not drawn. No stage direction.

F1.note: First draft warm and short. The correction (barn, 6pm, cast and crew only) holds on turns two and three; the three-line version is exactly three lines and carries the date and the RSVP. No address in the group-chat version.

F2.note: Corrections: both are preserved. After turn two the insurance is never raised again and the river and scene 19 never reappear; turn three is two paragraphs of prose to Hannah. Turn one: the insurance risk and the barn-Thursday risk to scene 22 are real memo risks. The scene 19 risk is argued from 'Daniel departs on Wednesday', but the memo says only that he must leave the set by 3pm Wednesday for an evening stage call; it does not say he is unavailable Thursday, and the memo's own scene 19 risks (Grace's 7am river measurement, the two-hour rehearsal, the Friday backup) are not used. Daniel's 3pm exit against scenes 12 and 15 is not among the three. Turns two and three: scene 15 is a dusk scene and Daniel leaves at 3pm Wednesday, so it cannot be shot on Wednesday at all and must go on Tuesday; turn two says his departure 'leaves very little room for Scene 15', and turn three tells Hannah 'we need to ensure Scene 15 is captured before Daniel's 3pm departure on Wednesday', which contradicts the supplied dusk requirement. Scene 9 on Tuesday as a single point of failure is sound. Turn two's risk 1 groups scenes 12, 14 and 22 correctly as barn work.
